steps.text: Remember to talk to your child about how to keep themselves safe in public places. Be extra careful on roads and always stay in sight of your grown up.

details.name: Outdoor Safety
details.nameForContentDev: Outdoor safety (minus Clever Never Goes link)

text:
Preparation:

Take a walk outside, it could be in a garden, park or just down the street. Try to find three interesting things to bring back with you.

The Activity:

Imagine you are a museum creator – this is a person who looks after the objects in a museum, chooses how they are displayed, and helps to explain what they are and why they are important. The three objects you found on your walk are going to be the objects in your museum.

  1. Display your objects. You could set them out on a table with labels saying what they are (or you might have another idea).
  2. Imagine you are going to take someone on a tour of your museum. What will you tell them about each object? You could make notes to help you remember.
  3. Show someone your objects. Explain who you are and welcome them to the museum, then take them to see the three objects and tell your guest all about them.


What if an object isn’t very interesting and I don’t know what to say?

Perhaps you found a leaf on your walk. What could you say?

  • You could decide to be scientific and talk about the kind of plant it is from and why leaves are important to plants.
  • You could invent a story that explains why the leaf is important – maybe the King of Persia plucked this leaf from the magical Oolibub tree and it flew with him across the earth and carried him to meet the famous talking snake of Durble.
  • You could think about it as a work of art – perhaps it represents the changing seasons and the particular colours of the leaf are important because of the way they show the warmth of the sun on an autumn day.
